videos.title: How to Finally Get What You Want in Life (It Takes 3 Things)
videos.description:
You made the vision board. You said the affirmations. You wrote it all down. And nothing changed.

In this episode, Jay Shetty takes apart the seven myths of manifestation that keep people stuck. He explains why your brain works like a GPS, not a genie, and why positive thinking is fuel but not the vehicle.

He shares the one step to pair with every affirmation, why writing a goal down is only the start, and why struggle often means you are on the right path, not the wrong one.

And he tells the story of the TV show every network rejected, and what that rejection made possible.

Learn what manifestation really is: clarity, belief and consistent action in alignment.

videos.title: Happiness Isn't the World's Job | Eckhart Tolle
videos.description:
Eckhart Tolle is a world-revered spiritual teacher and author known for sharing practical tools that allow people to experience life more richly.

During the podcast we discuss, and Eckhart demonstrates, how you can access greater inner peace, authenticity, creativity, and connection in your everyday life.

Eckhart also shares tools for quieting compulsive thinking, accessing inner stillness, and adopting a helpful mental vantage point when life gets challenging.

We also discuss how to balance your pursuit of external goals with your spiritual growth and relationships and, in doing so, foster a deeper sense of well-being.

This was a remarkable podcast discussion, thanks to him! you’ll come away with numerous practical tools. We also discuss aspects of merging a spiritual stance in life with culture and nature, and the forces that none of us escape.

It was an honor and pleasure to host you Eckhart Tolle!

Thank you for the work you do!

If anyone has questions or comments, please put them in the comments section below, and as always thank you for your interest in science!

videos.title: How Your Family Installed Your Triggers
videos.description:
Going home for the holidays is the fastest way to find out how much work you still have left to do. You can spend years in therapy learning your triggers, then walk through your parents' door and feel all of it slip away before dinner.

Understanding a pattern in your head and acting differently inside it are two separate skills, and the second one only gets built in the room with your family.

videos.title: When Telling the Truth Does More Harm Than Good
videos.description:
Being honest doesn’t mean saying every true thing the moment you think it. If the other person isn’t ready to hear it, or the truth would only cause pain without telling them anything useful, it can do as much damage as staying quiet.

Research even shows that small, kind lies told for someone’s benefit can increase trust, even when the person knows you’re doing it. And if “I’m just being honest” is your go-to defense, it might be worth asking whether you’re being honest or just being an asshole.
